title: Participant Outcomes Index - An Original Measure Built on Observable Behaviour
situation: Financial wellness measurement across the industry relied on self-reported readiness surveys. Those measures were unreliable, expensive to collect, and could not be tracked at scale or acted on at the participant level.
obstacle: Building a credible alternative required academic rigour the business did not have in-house, and required defining financial health in a way that measured behaviour rather than circumstance. A participant's income is not something they control. What they do with it is.
actions: Led the research partnership with Boston College to develop the Participant Outcomes Index
Built the measure exclusively on observable behavioural data rather than self-reported survey input
Framed the measure around whether a participant is doing everything available to them to position themselves for financial health, rather than measuring readiness
Incorporated the content into Plan Reviews
Presented it to many top clients for feedback and validation
results: Produced a measure differentiated from anything competitors were running
Content incorporated into Plan Reviews and shown to major clients for feedback
Product built, with marketing and deployment planning in progress at departure
fullStory: Everyone in the industry measured financial wellness by asking people how ready they felt. That produces a number you cannot act on and cannot track. I led a partnership with Boston College to build something different: a measure of financial health constructed only from observable behaviour. The framing matters. It does not measure whether someone is ready, because readiness is mostly a function of income and circumstance. It measures whether they are doing everything available to them to position themselves. That is the part a plan sponsor can influence. We built the product, put the content into Plan Reviews, and took it to many of our top clients for feedback. Marketing and deployment planning were still underway when I left. Ovation Award in 2025.
notes: USAGE WARNING: At departure the Participant Outcomes Index was built, incorporated into Plan Reviews, and validated with clients. Marketing and deployment planning were in progress. Do not describe it as launched, deployed, or rolled out. The research partner was Boston College.
